newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.12 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.12 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 1.12 percent on Wednesday in continued selective activity as the market overcame resistance awaited at 1,170, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,178, up 13 points from Tuesday's previous record of 1,165. In dollar terms, it rose to a record of $1.05 from Tuesday's $1.04.
Trade volume dropped to 20.17 trillion lira ($179.5 million) from previous 21.14 trillion ($189.1 million).
"The market continues its uptrend with intermittent profit-taking and share-based activity," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.

Two-day gains totalled 3.7 percent since Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the rally sparked by lower money and bond market rates, a quiet dollar and 1996 profit prospects of companies since the beginning of 1997.
The index had surged 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consequtive days after the market reopened on January 2, following a five-day holiday.
